profile.address: 739, Welch Drive, Medford, Jackson County, Oregon, 97501
profile.reading:
Data Center West, Inc. is an independent, privately held colocation and cloud-services provider that has operated in Oregon's Rogue Valley since 2004. Rather than build for a national hyperscale market, the company positions itself as the largest independent colocation and computing provider in Southern Oregon and Northern California, serving customers in Medford, Ashland, Klamath Falls and Grants Pass, and maintaining the Ashland Fiber Network as part of its regional connectivity.

This facility sits at 739 Welch Drive in Medford, Jackson County, and is the company's primary technical site. Per Data Center West's own published specifications, the Medford building offers roughly 2,000 square feet of climate-controlled, Level 1-connected technical space rated to a 500-pound-per-square-foot floor load, with racks that are seismically braced against earthquake movement, a meaningful design choice in an active seismic region. Backup power is supplied by a 600-amp diesel generator, a Caterpillar 3412 unit, and cooling runs through four to seven tons of redundant HVAC capacity. The company advertises diverse-route, redundant fiber connections and round-the-clock network monitoring, and offers customers a mix of rack, cabinet and cage space on a telco-neutral basis, meaning tenants can bring their own carrier of choice rather than being tied to one upstream provider.

Data Center West also operates a second, smaller facility roughly 175 miles north in Eugene, about 500 square feet, with a direct fiber connection into the city's Central Office 53, along with additional sites in Ashland, Oregon and Redding, California. Some third-party data-center directories list the Medford building under an Eugene-market heading, which can make the two sites easy to conflate; the facility described here, however, is the Medford location on Welch Drive, not the smaller Eugene site.

No independent power-capacity figure in megawatts has been published for the Medford facility, and the company does not disclose a power-usage-effectiveness rating, tenant list, or a breakdown of raised-floor versus support square footage, the kind of detail typically reserved for hyperscale or wholesale colocation providers rather than a regional, privately held operator serving a mid-size metro market. What is public is consistent with a modest, purpose-built regional colocation facility rather than a large multi-tenant data-center campus, and the company's emphasis on seismic bracing, generator backup and redundant fiber reflects the priorities of a business-continuity-focused provider serving small and mid-size enterprise customers across Southern Oregon.

profile.research_note:
Per operator's own building-spec page: Medford OR facility is 2,000 sqft technical space, 500lbs/sqft floor load, 600 AMP service with Caterpillar 3412 diesel generator (no MW figure published).

[2026-09-04 follow-up] This row's OSM-derived name reads 'Date Center West - Eugene' but its stored coordinates/address resolve to 739 Welch Drive, Medford OR -- Data Center West's primary Medford facility, not the company's actual Eugene site. Per the operator's own facilities page (datacenterwest.com/our-facilities.html), Data Center West operates a SEPARATE, smaller ~500 sqft Eugene facility with direct fiber to Eugene Central Office 53, plus sites in Ashland OR and Redding CA. Third-party directories (lead only, not cited) list a distinct Eugene address (800 Willamette St) different from this row's Medford coordinates. Conclusion: this appears to be an OSM mistagging/duplicate -- an Eugene-derived name attached to Medford coordinates -- rather than confirmation of a genuine second Medford-area Data Center West location marketed under an Eugene label. The public reading above describes the Medford facility the row's actual address represents and clarifies the naming discrepancy for readers without asserting this row IS the company's Eugene site.

reading.body:
This facility is a 2,000 square-foot regional colocation site in Medford, Oregon, not a hyperscale campus. The operator publishes no total power capacity in megawatts, only that the site runs on a 600-amp diesel generator with four to seven tons of HVAC redundancy, which suggests a modest single-building operation serving small and mid-size enterprise customers across Southern Oregon rather than a platform designed for large-scale AI workloads. Without a published power figure, this site cannot be ranked against other Oregon facilities or contribute to estimates of the state's AI-ready infrastructure.

Data Center West emphasizes business continuity features—seismic bracing, redundant fiber, round-the-clock monitoring, and telco-neutral connectivity—consistent with a regional provider protecting customer uptime rather than optimizing for compute density. The 500-pound-per-square-foot floor load and modest square footage do not disclose whether this building holds racks or cabins, or what fraction is technical space versus support areas. No power-usage-effectiveness rating or tenant list is published.

Oregon has published power capacity of 156.6 MW across 8 of its 133 mapped data centers. This facility, with no published megawatt figure, does not enter that count. It ranks ninth in the state only by mapping order, not by capacity. For a reader assessing whether grid constraints bind AI scaling in Oregon, this site contributes no measurable data to that question.
